reconcile.note: Keil and Delitzsch read the Genesis 35 naming as Jacob renewing the Bethel name he had already given the site on his outward journey, not a second founding.

discrepancy.note: Colenso treats the two Bethel-namings as independent Elohist and Jehovist accounts, each unaware of the other's earlier naming.

quotes.text: In E (xxxv.l5), Jacob gives the name 'Bethel' to the 'place where God spake witli him,' after liis return to Canaan from Padan-Aram … in X (xxviii.19), Jacob gives the name 'Bethel' to the place where Jehovah appeared to him twenty years previou.sly, when he was on his way to Padan-Aram
quotes.attr: John William Colenso (d. 1883), The Pentateuch and Book of Joshua Critically Examined, Vol. V (1865), ch. VI, on Genesis 28:19 and Genesis 35:15.

sides.snippet: He called the name of that place Bethel, but the name of the city was Luz at the first.
sides.verseText: He called the name of that place Bethel, but the name of the city was Luz at the first.

sides.snippet: He built an altar there, and called the place El Beth El
sides.verseText: He built an altar there, and called the place El Beth El; because there God was revealed to him, when he fled from the face of his brother.
